title: Two-phase study overview
caption: The two phases share a research motivation but differ in task, observation unit, and analysis. Phase 2 is a methodological extension rather than a direct performance comparison or replication.

title: Private-guess/shared-feedback loop
caption: Illustrative three-agent sum-mode loop. The evaluator observes guesses and the hidden target; each agent receives its own history and shared categorical feedback. Correct feedback terminates the game.

title: Phase 2 execution and artifact architecture
caption: A sweep invokes a policy adapter that requests one action at a time from the model, using shared task state and a supplied valid-action list. The environment validates and applies actions; canonical episode records support exports and analysis. Nominal actors are not separate persistent agent contexts.

title: Action-selection and validation boundaries
caption: Policy validation rejects or retries model responses before actions reach the environment. The 96 recoverable invalid responses in final traces are distinct from zero invalid environment calls. Allow-list selection exposes exact patch replacements, so patch acceptance measures compliance within a constrained interface.

title: Balanced matched-assignment study design
caption: The final run covers 16 engineered fixture variants and four repetitions per policy–variant cell. The three policies share fixture/repetition/seed identities, yielding 64 episodes per policy and 192 completed episodes. Shared seed identities do not make model responses deterministic.

title: Policy and actor-assignment comparison
caption: Single-agent actions use actor 0. Independent mode alternates actor IDs by adapter rule; prompted coordination lets one action-selection process choose the actor ID. Role wording and actor-assignment authority change together, preventing a prompt-only causal interpretation.

title: Action abstraction and information loss
caption: Tool events map to five action categories; a priority rule then assigns one per-agent profile. The two illustrative traces both become finalized, demonstrating how terminal-action priority masks prior retrieval, update, and verification. The example is conceptual, not an observed episode sequence.

title: Scripted pilot outcomes
caption: The 80-episode scripted pilot recorded 54 successes, 22 partials, and four failures. The three non-random policies shared 16/20 success outcomes; the random valid-action policy had 6/20. These are pipeline checks, not LLM treatment estimates.

title: Final outcomes and marginal success-rate intervals
caption: The final dataset contains 187 successes and five partial outcomes, with no failures. Dots and whiskers show success rates and two-sided 95% Wilson intervals calculated from reported counts. Marginal Wilson intervals do not adjust for repeated fixtures; they are not a paired policy comparison.

title: Matched-policy success-rate contrasts
caption: Point differences use matched reported outcomes. Whiskers reproduce the report’s 95% fixture-variant cluster bootstrap intervals (10,000 resamples); all include zero. These intervals were not independently rerun from episode-level data, and no causal or superiority claim follows.

title: Tool-call volume and composition
caption: Stacked bar lengths are mean calls per final episode, calculated by dividing each reported tool count by 64. Totals are 6.50, 6.16, and 5.80 calls. Fewer calls alone do not demonstrate greater efficiency because five episodes stopped with unresolved defects.

title: Premature finalization in the five partial episodes
caption: The reported partial episodes finalized after 4–6 calls despite a 12-call limit. Discount-order cases left the primary defect unresolved; invoice-total cases left the tertiary defect unresolved. Case A/B are display labels, not episode IDs. Bars show stopping positions only, not intermediate action histories.

title: First-attempt completion and collection burden
caption: The first sweep completed 169/192 manifest IDs; 23 initially failed IDs eventually completed. Whole-episode restarts produced 56 failed-attempt records and 248 total executions. The final task-outcome sample remains 192 episodes. Lower-panel red segments count failed attempts, not task failures.

title: Exploratory MI estimates and eligibility sensitivity
caption: Whiskers reproduce the reported 500-resample percentile intervals; p-values are from 250 unrestricted outcome permutations. The diamond retains all 64 coordinator episodes by adding no_actions profiles and has no reported interval. These diagnostics neither compare policies inferentially nor establish coordination.

title: Joint-profile/outcome frequency distributions
caption: Each profile pair is ordered agent 0 / agent 1. Green denotes success (S), amber partial (P). Independent-policy partials occupy all three observed cells (2, 1, 1); the coordinator paired sample has one partial in finalized/updated. Every pair includes finalized, exposing the terminal-actor component of the encoding.

title: Actor workload and tool-mix attribution
caption: Pooled actor shares and mean per-episode imbalance are different summaries. Prompted coordination has greater mean imbalance and tool-mix TVD, but it also permits model-selected actor attribution. TVD excludes six single-active coordinator episodes. These results do not demonstrate emergent specialization.

title: Fixture-family success counts by condition
caption: Each cell contains eight episodes: two fixture variants × four repetitions. Billing success counts were 8/8, 4/8, and 7/8; all seven other families had 8/8 successes in each condition. These engineered families are not a random sample of software-repair tasks.

title: Synthetic state transitions and terminal outcomes
caption: A fresh fixture enters an in-progress state as actions make task progress. Finalization or budget exhaustion triggers classification using predefined defect and regression rules. Synthetic success is an environment outcome, not proof that executed software was repaired.
